points.description: States that the height of a tree is the length of the longest path from the root down to a leaf (the deepest leaf), measured in edges/levels. Wording may differ.
points.partial_credit: Half or more of the marks for a vague or partly correct idea, e.g. 'depth/number of levels of the tree' or 'path from root to a leaf' without 'longest'.

points.description: Makes clear the path runs from the root to a leaf (any/farthest leaf), not just between arbitrary nodes.
points.partial_credit: Half if only one endpoint (root or leaf) is mentioned.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying the height is the length of the longest root-to-leaf path, in any wording. Part marks for vague or incomplete versions such as 'number of levels' or a root-to-leaf path with no mention of longest. No marks for answers about other things such as node count or the definition of depth of a single node without the longest root-to-leaf idea.
